aspects.says: A wrapper keeps the original exception and its stack trace only if it is passed the cause, so the (message, cause) constructor is the one never to leave out.
basis: section:A Wrapper Keeps the Original Failure Only If It Is Given the Cause

aspects.says: The (cause) constructor takes cause.toString() as its message.
basis: section:A Wrapper Keeps the Original Failure Only If It Is Given the Cause

aspects.says: An exception without a stack trace prints no at lines, so a failure that leaves the code is an ordinary exception with the miss as cause.
basis: section:Filling In the Stack Trace Is Most of the Cost; Skip It Only Where Nobody Reads the Trace

aspects.says: writableStackTrace = false (or an overridden fillInStackTrace) skips the stack walk that makes up most of an exception's cost, so it suits exceptions used as control flow that never leave the code that catches them.
basis: section:Filling In the Stack Trace Is Most of the Cost; Skip It Only Where Nobody Reads the Trace

aspects.says: A checked custom exception that a method lets escape must be declared, or the code does not compile.
basis: section:The Class You Extend Decides Who Must Handle It
aspects.reason: a rule the compiler enforces has no wrong solution that compiles, so no test can grade it; the page shows the compiler error

aspects.says: Context goes in final fields for code and in the message for the log, because toString() and the stack trace show only the class name and the message.
basis: section:Context Goes in Final Fields and in the Message

aspects.says: Every exception is Serializable, so a non-serializable field makes serializing it fail, and transient loses the data.
basis: section:Every Exception Is Serializable, So Its Fields Must Be Too

aspects.says: An exception class can't be generic, and neither can an inner class of a generic class; a record can't be an exception.
basis: section:An Exception Class Can't Be Generic

aspects.says: An exception sent between releases declares its own serialVersionUID, or a change in the class's shape makes it unreadable.
basis: section:Every Exception Is Serializable, So Its Fields Must Be Too

aspects.says: Extending Exception makes an exception checked and extending RuntimeException makes it unchecked; extending Throwable directly escapes every catch (Exception e).
basis: section:The Class You Extend Decides Who Must Handle It
